column1: An emerging discipline called neuroaesthetics is seeking to bring scientific objectivity to the study of art, and has already given us a better understanding of many masterpieces.
column2: 一门名为神经美学的新兴学科，正试图把科学的客观性引入艺术研究，而且已经帮助我们更深入地理解许多杰作。

column1: The blurred imagery of Impressionist paintings seems to stimulate the brain’s amygdala, for instance.
column2: 例如，印象派画作中朦胧的画面似乎会刺激大脑的杏仁核。

column1: Since the amygdala plays a crucial role in our feelings, that finding might explain why many people find these pieces so moving.
column2: 由于杏仁核在情感活动中起着关键作用，这项发现也许能解释为什么很多人觉得这些作品如此动人。
column3: plays a crucial role|起着关键作用

column1: Could the same approach also shed light on abstract twentieth-century pieces, from Mondrian’s geometrical blocks of colour, to Pollock’s seemingly haphazard arrangements of splashed paint on canvas?
column2: 同一研究方法能否帮助我们认识20世纪的抽象作品呢？比如蒙德里安的几何色块，或是波洛克在画布上泼洒出来、看似杂乱无章的颜料布局。
column5: geometrical blocks of colour|几何色块

column1: Sceptics believe that people claim to like such works simply because they are famous.
column2: 怀疑者认为，人们之所以声称喜欢这类作品，仅仅是因为作品很有名。

column1: We certainly do have an inclination to follow the crowd.
column2: 我们的确有从众的倾向。

column1: When asked to make simple perceptual decisions such as matching a shape to its rotated image, for example, people often choose a definitively wrong answer if they see others doing the same.
column2: 例如，让人们作简单的知觉判断，如把一个形状与它旋转后的图形配对时，倘若看到别人选择一个明显错误的答案，他们往往也会选同一个。
column7: doing the same|作同样的选择

column1: It is easy to imagine that this mentality would have even more impact on a fuzzy concept like art appreciation, where there is no right or wrong answer.
column2: 不难想象，这种心理对艺术欣赏这样界线模糊的概念可能影响更大，因为这里的答案无所谓对错。

column1: Angelina Hawley-Dolan, of Boston College, Massachusetts, responded to this debate by asking volunteers to view pairs of paintings - either the creations of famous abstract artists or the doodles of infants, chimps and elephants.
column2: 马萨诸塞州波士顿学院的安吉莉娜·霍利-多兰为研究这一争论，请志愿者观看成对的画作。这些画有的出自著名抽象艺术家之手，有的则是婴儿、黑猩猩和大象的涂鸦。

column1: They then had to judge which they preferred.
column2: 接着，志愿者要判断自己更喜欢其中哪一幅。

column1: A third of the paintings were given no captions, while many were labelled incorrectly - volunteers might think they were viewing a chimp’s messy brushstrokes when they were actually seeing an acclaimed masterpiece.
column2: 三分之一的画作没有标注说明，另有许多标错了。志愿者可能以为眼前是黑猩猩凌乱的笔触，实际上看到的却是广受赞誉的杰作。

column1: In each set of trials, volunteers generally preferred the work of renowned artists, even when they believed it was by an animal or a child.
column2: 在每组试验中，志愿者通常都更喜欢著名艺术家的作品，即使他们以为那是动物或孩子画的。

column1: It seems that the viewer can sense the artist’s vision in paintings, even if they can’t explain why.
column2: 看来，观者可以感受到画中艺术家的构想，即便说不出原因。

column1: Robert Pepperell, an artist based at Cardiff University, creates ambiguous works that are neither entirely abstract nor clearly representational.
column2: 卡迪夫大学的艺术家罗伯特·佩珀雷尔创作的画意象模糊，既非全然抽象，也不具有明确可辨的具象形态。

column1: In one study, Pepperell and his collaborators asked volunteers to decide how ‘powerful’ they considered an artwork to be, and whether they saw anything familiar in the piece.
column2: 在一项研究中，佩珀雷尔和合作者请志愿者判断一件艺术作品有多强的“感染力”，以及能否从中看出熟悉的事物。

column1: The longer they took to answer these questions, the more highly they rated the piece under scrutiny, and the greater their neural activity.
column2: 回答这些问题花的时间越长，志愿者就越看好正在审视的作品，神经活动也越强。

column1: It would seem that the brain sees these images as puzzles, and the harder it is to decipher the meaning, the more rewarding is the moment of recognition.
column2: 大脑似乎把这些画面当成一道道谜题。含义越难破译，看懂的那一刻就越令人满足。
column7: moment of recognition|豁然看懂的那一刻

column1: And what about artists such as Mondrian, whose paintings consist exclusively of horizontal and vertical lines encasing blocks of colour?
column2: 那蒙德里安这类艺术家呢？他的画完全由水平和垂直的线条构成，线条围住了一块块颜色。

column1: Mondrian’s works are deceptively simple, but eye-tracking studies confirm that they are meticulously composed, and that simply rotating a piece radically changes the way we view it.
column2: 蒙德里安的作品看似简单，眼动追踪研究却证实，他的构图经过精心安排；即使只是把画转个角度，我们观看它的方式也会发生根本改变。

column1: With the originals, volunteers’ eyes tended to stay longer on certain places in the image, but with the altered versions they would flit across a piece more rapidly.
column2: 观看原作时，志愿者的目光往往在画面的某些位置停留更久；观看调整过方向的版本时，目光则会更快地在画面上掠过。

column1: As a result, the volunteers considered the altered versions less pleasurable when they later rated the work.
column2: 结果，后来给作品打分时，志愿者认为改动后的版本不那么令人愉悦。

column1: In a similar study, Oshin Vartanian of Toronto University asked volunteers to compare original paintings with ones which he had altered by moving objects around within the frame.
column2: 在一项类似研究中，多伦多大学的奥欣·瓦塔尼安移动画框内的物体，改动画作，再请志愿者将原画和改动后的版本相比较。
column7: within the frame|在画框范围内

column1: He found that almost everyone preferred the original, whether it was a Van Gogh still life or an abstract by Miró.
column2: 他发现，无论梵高的静物画还是米罗的抽象画，几乎人人都更喜欢原作。

column1: Vartanian also found that changing the composition of the paintings reduced activation in those brain areas linked with meaning and interpretation.
column2: 瓦塔尼安还发现，改变画的构图会使大脑中与意义和阐释有关的区域激活程度下降。

column1: In another experiment, Alex Forsythe of the University of Liverpool analysed the visual intricacy of different pieces of art, and her results suggest that many artists use a key level of detail to please the brain.
column2: 在另一项实验中，利物浦大学的亚历克斯·福赛思分析了不同艺术品的视觉复杂程度。她的结果表明，许多艺术家会采用某种恰到好处的细节密度，让大脑感到愉悦。
column7: key level of detail|恰到好处的细节程度
column8: please the brain|使大脑感到愉悦

column1: Too little and the work is boring, but too much results in a kind of ‘perceptual overload’, according to Forsythe.
column2: 福赛思说，细节太少，作品就显得乏味；细节太多，又会造成某种“知觉过载”。

column1: What’s more, appealing pieces both abstract and representational, show signs of ‘fractals’ - repeated motifs recurring in different scales.
column2: 此外，吸引人的作品无论是抽象还是具象，都显示出“分形”的迹象，也就是在不同尺度上反复出现的图形。

column1: Fractals are common throughout nature, for example in the shapes of mountain peaks or the branches of trees.
column2: 分形在自然界中十分常见，例如山峰的形状、树枝的形态都可见到。

column1: It is possible that our visual system, which evolved in the great outdoors, finds it easier to process such patterns.
column2: 人的视觉系统在户外自然环境中演化而来，处理这类模式或许更加容易。
column5: the great outdoors|户外自然环境

column1: It is also intriguing that the brain appears to process movement when we see a handwritten letter, as if we are replaying the writer’s moment of creation.
column2: 同样耐人寻味的是，看到手写字母时，大脑似乎会处理书写动作的信息，仿佛正在重演落笔者创作的那一刻。
column7: moment of creation|创作的那一刻

column1: This has led some to wonder whether Pollock’s works feel so dynamic because the brain reconstructs the energetic actions the artist used as he painted.
column2: 这使一些人猜想，波洛克的画之所以显得充满动感，会不会是因为大脑重构了画家作画时那些充满力量的动作。

column1: This may be down to our brain’s ‘mirror neurons’, which are known to mimic others’ actions.
column2: 这或许要归因于大脑里的“镜像神经元”，人们已知这类神经元会模拟别人的动作。

column1: The hypothesis will need to be thoroughly tested, however.
column2: 不过，这个假说还需要充分检验。

column1: It might even be the case that we could use neuroaesthetic studies to understand the longevity of some pieces of artwork.
column2: 我们甚至可能借助神经美学研究，了解为什么某些艺术作品能长久流传。

column1: While the fashions of the time might shape what is currently popular, works that are best adapted to our visual system may be the most likely to linger once the trends of previous generations have been forgotten.
column2: 一时的风尚也许决定了当下流行什么，可当以往世代的潮流被人遗忘时，最有可能流传下来的，或许是那些最适合我们视觉系统的作品。
column3: fashions of the time|一时的风尚

column1: It’s still early days for the field of neuroaesthetics - and these studies are probably only a taste of what is to come.
column2: 神经美学仍处于起步阶段，这些研究很可能只是未来成果的初步预示。
column5: only a taste of|只是……的初步预示
column6: what is to come|未来将出现的事物

column1: It would, however, be foolish to reduce art appreciation to a set of scientific laws.
column2: 不过，把艺术欣赏简化为一套科学定律，未免愚蠢。

column1: We shouldn’t underestimate the importance of the style of a particular artist, their place in history and the artistic environment of their time.
column2: 我们不能低估特定艺术家的个人风格、在历史中的位置以及其所处时代的艺术环境的重要性。
column5: place in history|在历史中的位置

column1: Abstract art offers both a challenge and the freedom to play with different interpretations.
column2: 抽象艺术既带来挑战，也给了我们自由尝试多种阐释的空间。

column1: In some ways, it’s not so different to science, where we are constantly looking for systems and decoding meaning so that we can view and appreciate the world in a new way.
column2: 从某些方面看，它与科学颇为相似。在科学中，我们也不断寻找系统、解读意义，以便用新的方式观看并欣赏这个世界。
column3: In some ways|从某些方面看
